name: ESP32-C6-DevKitC-1-N8 (Espressif)
sources: ESP32-C6 Series Datasheet v1.5 (2026-03-31): CPU, memory, radios, ADC, UART, security, current; ESP32-C6-DevKitC-1 v1.2 user guide (esp-dev-kits, docs.espressif.com) and schematic v1.4 (PDF on dl.espressif.com): board parts, J1 and J3 headers, J5, CP2102N-A02 bridge; all read 2026-10-07

columns.head: The chip: ESP32-C6
items: Processor: RISC-V, 32-bit
One main core at up to 160 MHz, plus a small 20 MHz low-power core for jobs while the main one sleeps
Flash: 8 MB
In the ESP32-C6-WROOM-1 module, outside the chip. Code runs from it through a 32 kB cache
RAM: 512 kB
Working memory (plus 16 kB that stays on in deep sleep). Rarely the limit on this chip
Power: 3.3 V
The chip wants 3.0 to 3.6 V. The board makes it from USB 5 V; signal pins are 3.3 V

columns.head: Connections inside the chip
items: Radios: 3 on one antenna
Wi-Fi 6 (2.4 GHz), Bluetooth LE 5, and 802.15.4 for Zigbee and Thread. They take turns on the air
GPIO: 23 on the headers
Plain on/off pins, and any of them can carry UART, SPI or I2C through the pin switchboard
UART: 2 (+1 low-power)
Simple serial text, up to 5 Mbaud. UART0 (GPIO16, GPIO17) goes to the board's USB-to-UART chip
ADC: 1, 7 channels
Measures a voltage in 4,096 steps (12-bit), up to 100,000 times a second. No DAC to make one
Security blocks
AES, SHA, RSA and ECC math in hardware, and a true random number generator

columns.head: On the board, and missing
items: On the board
Two USB-C ports (the chip's own USB, and a USB-to-UART chip), BOOT and RESET buttons, one color LED (GPIO8), power LED
Headers
32 pins in two rows, J1 and J3. Fits a breadboard
Not on the board
No sensors. No USB cable in the bag. No separate debug probe needed: the chip's own USB does JTAG
Not on the chip
No FPU (floating point is done in software), no DAC
Watch out
GPIO4, 5, 8, 9 and 15 set the boot mode at reset; GPIO12 and 13 are the USB port's own wires
